ADVERTISEMENT

Host Your Next Off-Site at Harborview Suites

Harborview Suites offers meeting rooms and overnight accommodations for teams of 15 to 200. Each conference package includes a dedicated event coordinator, high-speed Wi-Fi, and a [[171]] catering menu that can be adjusted for dietary needs.
Book a two-night weekday stay by December 1 and receive 10% off that first room block. [[172]], standard seasonal rates apply to any additional events you hold later in the same year.

Call 555-0140 or visit www.harborview-suites.example to request a [[173]] proposal for your event. [[174]]

Harborview Suites — where business travel feels like a retreat.

questions.explanation: An adjective is needed before the noun phrase "catering menu." "Flexible" correctly modifies "menu."
questions.commonMistake: Choosing the adverb "flexibly" or the noun "flexibility" where an adjective slot is required.

questions.explanation: The next sentence describes the rate that applies after the first discounted booking. "Thereafter" marks that later time.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing "Otherwise," which would signal an alternative if the December 1 deadline is missed, not a later additional event.

questions.explanation: A proposal that covers rooms, catering, and services in full is "comprehensive" — complete and thorough.
questions.commonMistake: Confusing "comprehensive" (complete) with "comprehensible" (easy to understand) or "compulsory" (required).

passages.title: HR: open enrollment for health benefits

text.content:
Dear colleagues,

Open enrollment for next year’s health and dental plans will run from October 6 through October 24. All eligible employees must complete their selections in the benefits portal during this window.
Last year’s elections will roll forward automatically if you take no action. [[175]], dependents who aged out of coverage must be removed even if you keep the same medical plan.
Employees who miss the deadline will [[176]] last year’s plan by default and may not change coverage until the next qualifying life event.

Please complete your [[177]] by October 24 so that payroll deductions can be updated in November. [[178]]

Questions may be sent to benefits@pinnacle-retail.example.
Elena Vasquez
Benefits Administrator
Pinnacle Retail Group

questions.explanation: Automatic rollover is the default, but aged-out dependents still have to be removed. "Nevertheless" marks that exception.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing "Similarly" or "For instance," which do not signal a required exception to the rollover rule.

questions.explanation: To "retain last year’s plan" means to keep it. The sentence needs a transitive verb with "plan" as the object.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing "remain," which cannot take a direct object, or a look-alike (restrain / refrain) that does not mean "keep."

questions.explanation: After the possessive "your," a noun is required. "Enrollment" is the noun in "complete your enrollment."
questions.commonMistake: Using the verb "enroll" after "your," where a noun slot is needed.

CLEARWATER CHRONICLE — Staff News

Hybrid Work Schedule Begins in October

Clearwater Analytics will introduce a company-wide hybrid schedule on October 1. Under the new policy, most office staff will work from home two days each week and report to headquarters on the remaining three.

Early feedback from a summer pilot has been [[179]]. Teams reported higher focus on deep-work tasks and fewer late arrivals. [[180]], managers asked for clearer guidelines on which days entire teams must be on-site together.

Human Resources will publish an [[181]] calendar for each department by September 20. [[182]]

Employees with questions may contact hybrid@clearwater.example.

questions.explanation: Higher focus and fewer late arrivals are positive outcomes, so the feedback is "favorable" (encouraging or positive).
questions.commonMistake: Choosing a look-alike adjective (fragile / former / formal) that does not mean positive or promising.

questions.explanation: The managers' request for clearer guidelines contrasts with the otherwise positive pilot results. "However" marks that contrast.
questions.commonMistake: Using "Likewise" or "For instance" when the sentence introduces a concern, not a parallel or example.

questions.explanation: An adjective is needed before the noun "calendar." "Official" correctly modifies "calendar."
questions.commonMistake: Choosing the adverb "officially" or the noun "office" where an adjective slot before a noun is required.

passages.title: Operations: warehouse forklift and aisle safety

text.content:
MEMORANDUM

To: All warehouse associates
From: Operations Safety Office
Date: September 12
Subject: Updated forklift and aisle safety rules

Beginning September 22, all forklift operators must complete a refresher course before their next shift. Associates who miss the training will not be [[183]] to operate powered equipment until they are certified.
Yellow walkways must remain clear of pallets and packaging waste. [[184]] high-visibility vests are required in Zones B and C at all times, including during short breaks.

Supervisors should log any near-miss incidents within one hour. [[185]], they must close any aisle that becomes blocked until the hazard is removed. [[186]]

Thank you for helping keep the floor safe.
— Operations Safety Office

questions.explanation: After "will not be," a past-participle / adjective form is required. "Permitted" means allowed.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing the noun "permission" or the base verb "permit" where a be + adjective/participle slot is needed.

questions.explanation: Safety rules that apply "at all times" describe requirements that are "mandatory" (required), not optional.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing "Optional," which contradicts a rule that applies at all times including breaks.

questions.explanation: Closing a blocked aisle is an additional safety duty alongside logging near-misses. "Furthermore" adds that requirement.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing "Conversely," which would introduce an opposite idea rather than another rule.

text.content:
NOTICE

Annual Community Food Drive — October 6–10
Human Resources invites all employees to donate nonperishable food for the Metro Food Bank. Collection barrels will be placed in the lobby and on each floor near the elevators.
Barrels fill quickly during the lunch rush. [[187]], please drop off donations in the morning when possible.

Every department that fills at least one barrel will receive a [[188]] mention in the staff newsletter. Teams are encouraged to record their [[189]] on the sheet taped to each barrel. [[190]]

Drop-off ends at 4:00 P.M. on Friday, October 10. For volunteer shifts packing boxes on October 11, sign up at hr.example/fooddrive.
— Human Resources

questions.explanation: Morning drop-off is a logical response to barrels filling during lunch. "Therefore" marks that consequence.
questions.commonMistake: Using "In contrast" when there is no opposing idea, only a practical recommendation.

questions.explanation: An adjective is needed before the noun "mention." "Special" correctly modifies "mention."

questions.explanation: Teams record what they donate; "contributions" means donated items or gifts.
